content.thinking:
Okay, I've just spent a lot of effort setting up the overall project structure with a series of detailed tasks: installing dependencies, building config and leaderboard modules, hardware detection, model implementation, data pipeline, training loop, benchmark suite, SLERP merge, and the final train entry point. These tasks lay out the core engineering work needed to get the 1M‑parameter model training pipeline up and running, and they each have clear descriptions and deliverables.

Now I need to think about the higher‑level process governance that will keep this effort reliable and reproducible. The codebase will evolve rapidly as I implement each feature, and I want to ensure that any change to the training script—especially those that could affect model quality or performance—gets validated with a substantial test. The original plan (from the earlier context) mentions a “2B‑test rule”: any feature change must be tested with at least 2 billion tokens, and only one feature should be altered at a time to isolate its impact. This rule is crucial for tracking the effect of each modification and for maintaining a clean experiment log.

Looking back at the conversation, I haven't yet created any documentation that enforces or records this rule. The repository likely has an AGENTS.md file (or similar) that outlines guidelines for contributors, but it currently lacks the explicit 2B‑test requirement. Moreover, there’s no systematic way to log each test run, its commit hash, what change was made, whether the change was kept, a brief description, and the resulting scores (overall and efficiency). Without such a log, it will be hard to audit progress or reproduce results later.

Given the pattern I've been following—using TaskCreate calls to formalize each piece of work—I should create a new task that captures the need to edit AGENTS.md to include the 2B‑test rule and also to create a new scores.md file that will serve as a structured changelog for these experiments. This task should be concise but explicit: it must mention updating AGENTS.md with the rule that every training‑script feature change requires its own 2 B‑token test, enforcing one‑feature‑at‑a‑time testing; and it must set up scores.md with columns for commit ID, change description, whether the change was kept, a short description, and the relevant scores.

Creating this task now will keep the documentation work in sync with the technical tasks I've already queued, ensuring that the governance process is not forgotten as I dive into code. It also follows the same workflow I've been using: each major piece of work gets its own TaskCreate entry, making it easy to track progress and assign responsibility later.

Therefore, the next logical step is to issue a TaskCreate call that captures exactly this documentation effort.

arguments.subject: Edit AGENTS.md (2B-test rule) + create scores.md
arguments.description: AGENTS.md: every training-script feature change requires its own 2B-token test, one feature at a time. scores.md: commit ID + change + kept? + description + scores.
